text: WION (/ˈwi.ɑːn/, WEE-ahn; World is One News) is an Indian English-language news channel headquartered in Noida, India, owned by the Essel Group and part of the Zee Media network, whose majority owner is Subhash Chandra and family. As of 2021, WION had a presence in over 190 countries. The channel has faced scrutiny from foreign nations, including China and Canada, over its reporting, and in 2022 was temporarily blocked from YouTube for broadcasting a speech by Sergey Lavrov, the head of Russia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which violated YouTube's community guidelines. This block was lifted on 26 March 2022 after a social media campaign by WION. The channel's former Pakistan bureau chief, Taha Siddiqui, was forced into exile following a failed kidnapping attempt in Islamabad and was replaced by Anas Mallick, who resigned in July 2025. WION has been accused of promoting misinformation regarding COVID-19. Zee Media appointed Rohit Gandhi as the founder and first editor-in-chief in August 2015 to establish the channel, which launched its simulcast on its website and as a free-to-air satellite service on 15 June 2016, with television broadcasts beginning on 15 August 2016. The channel was made available on Google Assistant in 2020. Sudhir Chaudhary served as editor-in-chief after Gandhi until his departure in 2021. Palki Sharma Upadhyay served for four years before resigning in September 2022 and later filed a lawsuit against WION, claiming the unauthorized use of confidential and proprietary Zee information, demanding she continue working until December 2022 and pay ₹2 crores in damages; however, the Delhi High Court rejected the appeal, with the next hearing postponed to March 2023. In 2021, the appointment of M.J. Akbar, an Indian journalist and politician accused of sexual assault, as an "editorial consultant" sparked controversy, with over 150 journalists demanding his removal. The current team includes Sidhant Sibal of DD News, who joined in April 2018, Madhu Soman, who joined as chief business officer in 2022 and left in 2024, and Rohit Banerjee, who manages branded content. Molly Gambhir now leads the WION channel as the anchor of Gravitas and Gravitas Plus, replacing Palki Sharma, with other journalists including Digvijay Singh Deo, Shivan Chanana, Rabin Sharma, Ieshan Wani, Esha Hanspal, Priyanka Sharma, and Alyson le Grange. In 2020, the Chinese Embassy in India protested against WION for an interview with Joseph Wu, head of Taiwan's foreign relations, accusing it of promoting "Taiwan Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) separatist activities" and violating India's One-China policy, stating Taiwan is an inalienable part of China as per UN resolutions and urging WION to respect India's official stance. The Chinese government also blocked access to the WION website in 2020, confirmed by GreatFire.org, and previously criticized WION for coverage of what it described as a "cover-up" of the COVID-19 pandemic in China. In March 2020, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Zhao Lijian blocked WION on Twitter, and Chinese diplomats in India also criticized its reporting. In June 2020, the Global Times, linked to the Chinese Communist Party, named WION in an article advising it to think "independently." In July 2020, cable operators in Nepal suspended broadcasts of several Indian news channels, including WION, after airing a video deemed disrespectful to K. P. Sharma Oli, the Nepali prime minister and leader of the Nepal Communist Party; the ban was lifted after a month due to public backlash. In September 2024, a report from RRM Canada titled "Potential Foreign Information Manipulation, and Interference following PM Statement on Killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar" cited WION, finding that "Modi-aligned outlets amplified several state-supported narratives about Prime Minister Trudeau, Canada's High Commissioner to India, Canada's national security agencies, Canada's Punjabi Sikh diaspora, and Hardeep Singh Nijjar's political beliefs," noting the outlet's "massive digital footprint" and its significant reach to global and Canadian audiences.
